Maintenance Report — MNT-0003-002

Asset: WELL-0003 (SW-23 Well 003, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 20 Jan 2023 08:00 · Finished: 20 Jan 2023 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0003-0014 on 2023-01-19 Report written: 20 Jan 2023

What happened

The weekly manual inspection INS-0003-0014 at 12:00 on 2023-01-19 found crude oil on the pad: about 8.2% of the pad area, estimated 4.1 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.9 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 376 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 301 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 2.9 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0003-002 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.45% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0003-0066 showed the wellhead at 13.9 °C with the air at 8.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 14 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

maintenance.action: Replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0003-014

Asset: WELL-0003 (SW-23 Well 003, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 07 Jul 2024 08:00 · Finished: 14 Aug 2024 12:00 · Well stopped for this job: 916 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0003-0087 on 2024-07-04 Report written: 14 Aug 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0003-0087 showed the wellhead at 40.3 °C with the air at 32.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 36 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0003-020

Asset: WELL-0003 (SW-23 Well 003, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 16 Aug 2025 08:00 · Finished: 26 Aug 2025 15:00 · Well stopped for this job: 247 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0003-0145 on 2025-08-14 Report written: 28 Aug 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the wellhead was cold and the pump jack was straining with a heavy, uneven load. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0003-0145 showed the wellhead at 34.5 °C with the air at 32.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 8 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A worn plunger that let sand settle and lock the pump.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 5 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.
